publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Independently reviewed by a second agent; not human scholarly approval.

handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 59r, 59v, 60r was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first pass of all 84 manuscript verses. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. Duplicate annotation records were identical in page and rectangle; one record per verse was reused without changing annotations.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. Even lines are indented; lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: Every verse and first-reader note has been checked against the source by a separate agent. Observations record supported features and corrections; uncertainty records limits of the source evidence without automatic human escalation. The separate JSON ledger records each disposition and binds this candidate to the review report.

revisionDesc.change: First source pass covering all 84 verses and visible interventions in folios 59r, 59v, 60r; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

div.head: First-pass source notes
div.note: Enlarged N. Above sedeo a dark annotation reads provisionally i uenio spectator; the first small sign and exact function remain uncertain. A small dark stroke also lies at the right end of this area, not interpreted as verse text.

The darker final r of loquerer is visible. Independent enlargement confirms ueni tecumque; the first-pass uenite cumque was an editorial word-division error. Small vertical strokes at the join do not supply additional letters.
The baseline reads quam with an e above its vowel. Both are retained without asserting a deletion or replacement relation. The esset ending uses a schematic et sign.
A small dark eo-like annotation is above the end of faues. Its exact reading and function remain uncertain.
The l of lora is distinctly darker; the earlier state and hand are not recoverable from ink tone.

Several letters are darker: t in At, p of pelops, s and o in pisaeo, and xe at the end. A faint u-like trace follows axe and is retained under unclear rather than silently discarded or declared erased.
The baseline name appears ippodamea, with i above its latter vowel. The base e is uncertain; no h is supplied and no deletion is invented.

The baseline ending after refug remains et-like and locally unclear. A dark s stands above with an adjacent horizontal stroke. The image does not securely establish a cancellation or the intended resulting verb; both inscriptions remain without a reconstructed substitution. This is documented source uncertainty, not an unresolved editorial task.
A small t is above the beginning of amen following Tu, recorded as an addition completing tamen. The later es is dark.
The i in pallia stands above the line with a small insertion cue below.
The source reads maenalion atalantis; the final n of maenalion is darker. The names are not regularized from another witness.

Final s of fortes is darker. A horizontal stroke precedes ipse, whose final vowel has an a above it. The stroke is not assigned a deletion function; the supralinear vowel is retained as an annotation.
The parchment has a hole between quid and fiet; writing lies on either side. The spacing is represented schematically, without asserting that text was lost. No absent word is supplied.
The b of bene is darker than its neighbours; no hand or earlier reading is assigned.

The ending of faciet is legible: the e is brown and the t is darker. Unnecessary unclear markup around et has been removed. A thin vertical stroke marks the vicinity of mota/tabella; word division is editorial.
Final s in magis and aeris is darker. The initial vowel of ęstus has a descending cauda, now preserved instead of ae. The following line reads femineas.
Nigro stands above the leui area. Its function is not established by a deletion; it remains a manuscript annotation. Nearby small strokes are not made into lost letters.

The written et between ades and the following et sign is visibly crossed through. After fac, a faint a-like trace precedes dea; it is retained locally under unclear rather than silently omitted. Its textual or corrective function is uncertain.

Ruricilae has a locally uncertain i-like baseline vowel with o above; the exact relation of the small marks beneath it remains qualified. After cereri the round o has a distinct underdot and is encoded as canceled. The darker t and o of tenero and the visible qui remain. No expected que or reconstructed earlier wording is supplied.
The final s of ueneris is covered by a dark round stroke and remains uncertain; the m of maior is dark. No recoverable erased word is asserted.
In stands above the line between tempus and omne with an insertion cue. Initial o of omne is darker.
The b in iuuabit is darker.
Impos stands above the opening of inseruisse; it is recorded separately because no deletion of the baseline is established. The i near the end of cancellis is dark.
The e of quadriiuges is dark and s stands higher above it. The s is encoded as above-line addition; exact correction history is not claimed.
An o is above the vowel of baseline Quid. Both visible readings remain, without an asserted cancellation.
Ad stands above moto with an insertion cue. The a of axe is darker; both visible features are retained without inferring an erased reading.

A parchment hole separates fauimus and ignauo; spacing is schematic and no lost text is supplied. S of sed and the final e of reuocate are darker. The next word is qrites with a horizontal stroke through the q descender, represented schematically as q̵rites and expanded quirites. The first pass incorrectly assigned the dark letter to q and silently spelled out the abbreviation.

The end shows a darker gis-like group after to, a point, and a faint second gis-like remnant. Both groups are locally qualified. No deletion or recoverable erased reading is established; this remains documented image uncertainty rather than an editorial escalation.

The baseline atque carries underdots and et ne stands above: the supported replacement is encoded as subst with del and add. A dark l-like stroke after mota remains locally uncertain and is not expanded or assigned a deletion function.

The source begins Euoluat, with dark d in admissis. In the margin a marked agm-like form and discolor repeat the word order agmen discolor; the expansion is low certainty, and the annotation is not made a substitution.
The q of spatioque is darker.
Both Sīt and sīt carry nasal marks and are expanded Sint and sint. The t in the first group and the second group as a whole are darker.
Two points and a sweeping terminal flourish follow loco. The flourish is schematically represented as a metamark with unknown function rather than assigned a textual expansion.
The visible terminal point after the et sign in habet is retained; it was omitted in the first pass.
Independent enlargement clearly reads final manu, correcting the first-pass genu. The source letters are retained without harmonizing with another witness.
The final vowel of succinctę has a visible descending cauda. It is transcribed as e caudata; diane is retained as written.

A thin dark loop with an upward connector lies above the opening of Sordide. It is represented schematically as a metamark; its function is not established and it is not interpreted as a replacement vowel.
The vowel following ph in phębe has a descending cauda. This source form is retained; phoebus is not altered.
The u in nouae is darker than its surrounding letters. This visible ink distinction is encoded without identifying a hand or an earlier state.
